items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates, allow only bounded reversible growth within existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, and claims boundaries, and continue read-only security evidence work. Do not access credentials or private containers, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, or conduct external outreach.

Continue the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
